title: The triage refusal's 'turn off holds' advice does not unblock the held item
scope: Verified: an agent-created item on the team preset is refused with advice to run 'gw config policy.triage_required_for human'. Run verbatim: rc=0, new agent items stop being held, but the item that printed the advice is STILL needs-triage. Also 'gw config policy.triage_required_for []' is refused (the list validator demands non-empty strings), so there is no CLI way to turn the hold off at all - the solo preset only gets [] by writing config directly - and the advice substitutes 'human', which moves the hold onto human-created items rather than removing it. Fix: allow an empty list where empty is meaningful, print '[]' in the advice, and when the policy stops covering a creator kind, release existing holds for that kind (recorded as an event), so the printed command unblocks the item in front of you.

evidence.text: verified: printed command pasted into a real shell released the hold and the item advanced; board POST /api/config saves unrelated settings (200) and releases holds when triage is turned off (released:1); agent B approves agent A's item; --approve never offered to a creator

title: Every refusal's printed command must be tested by running it verbatim
scope: Six times tonight the product printed advice that did not fix the thing in front of the user (T-0039, T-0034, T-0041, T-0087, T-0098, T-0095.1). Each was caught only because a specific ticket demanded a run-it-verbatim test. Make it a standing test instead: enumerate the refusals the CLI can print (triage, move, claim, release, guard, repair, check, next), drive each into its refusal state on a scratch board, extract every backtick-quoted gw command from the text, run it through a real shell exactly as printed, and assert the refusal no longer applies. A new refusal should fail CI until it is covered.
